paper.title: Algorithm 787: Fortran subroutines for approximate solution of maximum independent stable set problems using GRASP

field: combinatorics and optimization (maximum independent set heuristic, GRASP)
stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 787.gz: a shar with Doc/Makefile, Doc/read.me, Fortran77/Drivers/Sp/{driver.f,RES,data}, Fortran77/Src/Sp/src.f)

claim.text: gmis (GRASP, seed 270001, look4 50, maxitr 1000) on the shipped sample instance (data: 50 nodes, 619 arcs) prints 'Size of indep set : 7', as in the shipped RES output block. Exact tolerance (tol_abs 0), fixed in the queue entry before any run. The value 7 is the known optimum stated in read.me.

values.name: size of indep set, sample instance, seed 270001

attempt: Reproduced at the registered claim (exact). Both passes (clean rebuilds of the unpacked tree, each run on the shipped sample instance) print 'Size of indep set : 7' at iteration 1, with the same independent set {5, 15, 16, 27, 31, 32, 45} as the shipped RES block. The archive as shipped did not produce a binary: the shar's heredoc is unquoted, so the shell expands $(FC) $(FFLAGS) $(OBJS_GMIS) at unpack time and the Makefile rule loses its prerequisites and compiler (make reports 'o: No such file' and exits 0 because the error is ignored; no gmis executable). The build was therefore run as three gfortran commands carrying out the rule the Makefile intends (FFLAGS=-O from the Makefile; FC=gfortran). No source or build file was edited before the build (build-only, manifests pre, mid and post compared). Caveat: the claim is weak: the integer 7 is the known optimum, reached on the first GRASP iteration, so any run that finds an optimum would pass it; the set comparison with RES is extra evidence, not part of the registered claim.

original_attempt.reason: the authors' Doc/Makefile, as unpacked from the shar, has an empty compile rule (FC, FFLAGS and OBJS_GMIS expanded to nothing by the unquoted heredoc), so make produces no gmis executable (gmis_binary=no). make's own exit status is 0 only because the error is marked ignored.
